subject: Lumenlytics GCP Private Offer — request to smooth redemption cadence and buffer
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@lumenlytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:34 -0800
Subject: Lumen PO and redemption cadence (private offer PO-8943)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for walking us through the private offer last week. Procurement is reviewing the draft PO (attached) and we have one operational ask before we sign: the redemption cadence in the private offer is currently front-loaded into Q1 2027. Given our expected product launch timing and initial usage uncertainty, we would prefer a smoothed redemption schedule across the next three quarters (Q1–Q3).

Two asks:
- Can Redwood accept a tiered redemption profile instead of the current front-load? Ideally something like: ~35–40% Q1, ~30–35% Q2, remainder Q3 — but we are flexible.
- Is it possible to add a short-term drawdown buffer (8–12%) for the first 60 days post-redemption so we don’t run into capacity throttles if usage spikes on our launch day? That would give us breathing room while we tune usage patterns.

We attached the draft PO (Lumen_PO_Q4_2026.pdf). Procurement would like to finalize terms this month. Please let us know whether these are acceptable and any impacts to pricing or marketplace settlement timing.

Thanks,
Samantha Cho
Head of Cloud Ops & Procurement
Lumenlytics

Attachments: Lumen_PO_Q4_2026.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@lumenlytics.com>
Cc: Lumenlytics Procurement <procurement@lumenlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:30:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: Lumen PO and redemption cadence (private offer PO-8943)

Hi Samantha — appreciate the clear ask and the PO.

Short answer: yes, we can accommodate a smoothed redemption profile and a short-term buffer, with a small operational caveat around marketplace settlement timing. I attached a draft "commit buffer" matrix that shows a few options and the downstream implications (billing amortization windows, marketplace reconciliation, and our fallback behavior if actual redemption materially exceeds the buffer).

Proposed option we can sign to move quickly:
- Tiered redemption: 40% Q1, 35% Q2, 25% Q3.
- Short-term buffer: 8% of the committed units available as a 60-day flexible pool post-redemption. If buffer used beyond 60 days we will convert to on-demand billings or trigger the next quarter's burn.

Impacts: this will not change the list price on the PO. For marketplace accounting, GCP redemption timing shifts the revenue recognition window slightly (we'll reconcile against Marketplace invoices in the next month). The attached spreadsheet highlights the settlement timing.

If that works I can route a brief amendment (DocuSign) and get internal alignment; I looped in procurement in case they want to confirm.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0129

Attachments: redwood-commit-buffer-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:02:03 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Lumen PO and redemption cadence (PO-8943) — need approval for 8% buffer

Laura/Markus — quick heads-up and ask. Lumenlytics is asking for a smoothed redemption cadence plus an 8–12% 60-day buffer. I proposed 8% in the reply to move fast (see below).

Why I recommend approving 8%: minimal revenue deferral exposure, reduces risk of customer churn at launch (they can spike usage without immediate billing surprises), and keeps the private offer moving. Worst-case we convert buffer overage to on-demand and reconcile the Marketplace invoice next month.

Questions for you:
- Opex/revenue recognition side: any red flags if we accept an 8% available pool?
- If acceptable, I will issue the amendment and the DocuSign and finalize with procurement.

Thread and attachments copied below.

Thanks,
Vivek

On Tue, 1 Dec 2026 at 09:12, Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@lumenlytics.com> wrote:
> (original message attached)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 12:05:20 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Lumen PO and redemption cadence (PO-8943) — need approval for 8% buffer

Vivek —

I’m comfortable approving an 8% buffer for the 60-day window provided we: (1) include explicit language that any usage beyond the buffer converts to on-demand rates and (2) we reconcile with Marketplace invoice in the next billing cycle. That should limit any revenue recognition ambiguity.

Markus — FYI on settlement timing; if you see any accounting issues call it out now. Otherwise I’ll approve and you can proceed with the amendment for signature.

Thanks,
Laura
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Lumen PO and redemption cadence (private offer PO-8943) — confirmed amendment

Hi Samantha — good news: Laura approved an 8% 60-day buffer and we’ll proceed with a tiered redemption profile. See the confirmed plan below and the attached amendment for signature.

Confirmed plan (to be added to PO-8943 amendment):
- Redemption profile: 40% Q1 2027, 35% Q2 2027, 25% Q3 2027.
- 60-day flexible buffer: 8% of total committed units available immediately post-redemption. Any buffer usage beyond 60 days will be billed at on-demand rates and reconciled on the next marketplace invoice.
- No change to list price or volume discounts on the PO.

Next steps:
1) I attached the PO amendment (Lumen_PO_Amendment_Docusign.pdf) and a link to the DocuSign powerform — please sign the amendment so we can finalize the private offer.
2) After signature we’ll confirm the redemption window with GCP Marketplace finance and share an invoice reconciliation date (target within 30 days).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=example-ds-link
Shared materials: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_drive_link

If you want slightly more buffer (10–12%), I can re-run internal approval with finance, but it will add ~24–48 hours to the turnaround.

Thanks — let me know if you want any language tweaks in the amendment.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
